reasoning_trace.value: The paper proposes a full-duplex RO-ISAC system based on wavelength division duplexing (WDD) with a hybrid single-carrier and multi-carrier (HSM) waveform. The system uses blue and green lights for downlink and uplink transmissions, respectively, and employs a pair of blue and green optical filters to avoid interference between the reflected downlink signal and the uplink signal.

The system mechanism is based on retroreflective optical ISAC (RO-ISAC), which equips the target with a corner cube reflector (CCR) to enhance light reflection. The HSM waveform consists of both pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) samples, allowing for flexible performance trade-off between communication and sensing.

The paper reports a downlink data rate of 125 Mb/s and an uplink data rate of 12.5 Mb/s, with a ranging root mean square error (RMSE) of less than 4 cm. The system achieves full-duplex transmission using WDD, and the HSM waveform enables flexible trade-off between communication and sensing performance.

The proposed system addresses the challenges of bidirectional transmission and waveform design in RO-ISAC systems. The use of WDD and HSM waveform enables full-duplex transmission and flexible performance trade-off, making it a promising solution for 6G mobile communication systems.
